title: Annotatio IV §.XVII close: not corporal under species but SPIRITUALLY; receive not sacrifice — stop before §.XVIII
pass_a_gloss: Nor any more is Christ said to exist under the species, neither in the bread, nor from the bread, nor with the bread. Christ is not there in the body, by natural abiding, existently and corporally, but SPIRITUALLY, powerfully, blessedly, in truth; According to which abiding He will not be absent, nor about to depart from His own, in whose hearts He dwells. Those alone therefore, not others, receive CHRIST in the Sacraments who are inwardly vivified by His spirit. For the rest, the body and blood of Christ ought to be perceived by the Faithful, but not sacrificed, or lifted up for the sake of veneration, or carried about (p. 1650).
pass_b_english: Christ is not said to exist under the species — not in, from, or with the bread — not there corporally by natural abiding, but SPIRITUALLY, powerfully, blessedly, in truth, dwelling in His people’s hearts.

Only those inwardly vivified by His Spirit receive Christ in the Sacraments; body and blood are to be perceived by the Faithful — not sacrificed, elevated for veneration, or carried about. Stop before §.XVIII.
source_text: Nihilo magis dici Christum sub speciebus existere, neque in pane, neque ex pane, neque cum pane. Non ibi esse Christum in corpore, naturali mansione, existenter & corporaliter, sed SPIRITUALITER, potenter, benedictè, in veritate; Secundum quam mansionem non aberit, neque abiturus sit à suis, in quorum cordibus habitat. Eos proinde solos, non alios CHRISTUM in Sacramentis recipere, qui intrinsècùs ejus spiritu vivificati sunt. Cæterum, corpus & sanguinem Christi à Fidelibus percipi debere, non autem sacrificari, aut venerationis causa, attolli, aut circumferri, pag. 1650.
